constraints.replacement_id_policy: canonical proposition local part; lowercase words joined by hyphens

input_annotations.exact: BES does not solve power problems by pooling data; if most individual studies are underpowered, aggregating them can strengthen support for the null or unconstrained alternative.
BES behaves similarly to meta-analysis in many settings: support for the correct hypothesis increases with larger sample sizes and more studies.
It does not behave like data pooling: adding more underpowered studies can amplify support for an alternative rather than rescue a true but weakly supported hypothesis.

original_proposition.body:
# BES behaves like pooled meta-analysis

Bayesian Evidence Synthesis behaves like pooled meta-analysis when aggregating
study evidence.

This proposition is intentionally broad enough to be contested by the existing
BES summaries: the literature notes similarity in some settings, while also
warning that BES is not data pooling and can diverge when studies are weak or
boundary-adjacent.
original_proposition.title: BES behaves like pooled meta-analysis

output_contract.write: a Half D proposition resynthesis draft JSON

review.rationale: The current proposition bundles two distinct claims: BES can behave similarly to meta-analysis in some settings, but BES is not data pooling and can diverge when studies are underpowered or boundary-adjacent. The mixed asserted/negated literature annotations are therefore better handled by resynthesizing the proposition into narrower condition-aware claims than by treating the negated annotations as simple disputes of one stable proposition.
